findings.note: The same false precedence sentence is duplicated in four operator-facing documents, so the per-shard reviews each saw only part of the problem and a fix that touches one copy leaves three. commands/review-pr-ready.md:26, commands/review-task-done.md:26, skills/review-pr-ready/SKILL.md:52 and skills/review-task-done/SKILL.md:50 all tell the operator that --shard-result and --cross-shard-result 'take precedence over a file of the same identity in resultsDir'. Only the cross-shard slot behaves that way (shardpack.go sets found.CrossShard = &cross, last write wins). For shard results, Discover appends the explicit path after the directory entries into found.Shards, and reviewmanifest.shardResultBlockers then raises 'duplicate shard result shard-<id>' the moment two results match the same shard hash. So following the documented workflow to override a stale in-tree result does not override it: it turns the gate red with a blocker whose text explains nothing about the flag the operator just used.

findings.note: Both plugin manifests were edited in this PR (version bumped to 0.9.0, FSM sentence appended) but their Go floor was left at the pre-existing, now-wrong value, so the repository states two different minimum Go versions to users. go.mod requires go 1.26 (with toolchain go1.27.0), and INSTALL.md:9, README.md:85 and package.json:52 say Go 1.26+; .claude-plugin/plugin.json:4, .codex-plugin/plugin.json:25, .agents/plugins/marketplace.json:9 and the runtime error messages in cli/metareview.js:28,36 still say Go 1.22+. A user who trusts the plugin description installs a toolchain that cannot build the fallback go run path.

findings.note: Checked whether the judge prompt/decoder seam disagrees across packages: TemplateStillPresentCalibration omits confidence from the requested JSON while TemplateStillPresentProduct asks for it, and judge.Parse routes still-present through its default branch. Both are safe. confOf() supplies 0 for an absent confidence, the still-present path never gates on a threshold (only match/adjudicate do, at kind.go:450 and kind.go:471), and every judge.Request built in kind.go uses a typed judge.Kind* constant, so no node kind can reach the default branch by accident.
